scope: Kernels and launchers changed by 38ce67a44 (fix/moe-router-nonfinite) plus the S1 slow-link kernels moved to kernels/src/slowlink_prefill.hip, plus the gfx942 BF16 MFMA GEMM source kernels/src/gemm_bf16_mfma.gfx942.hip (the 32x32-tile entry gemm_bf16_mfma_gfx942 and the few-row entries gemm_bf16_mfma_gfx942_rows16 / _rows16_x2, launched by Gpu::launch_gemm_bf16_mfma_tiled and Gpu::launch_gemm_bf16_mfma_rows16) with the metadata parity of its non-production PM twin (pm_twins), plus the llama3 RoPE kernels (rope.hip, rope_batched.hip; HIPF-193). hip_sources/pm_emitters/pm_images are the closed lists below, not a counted receipt: the tests derive their sizes from these lists. Launchers under crates/*/src, examples/, tests/ and benches/ are all checked; only the OLD-ABI call variants in old_variants are exempt, one per call.

kernels/gemm_bf16_mfma_gfx942_rows16_pm_.reason: Committed gfx942 PeaceMaker twin of the two HIP few-row entries: same symbol names and the same 104-byte kernarg ABI (nine 8-byte pointers X, A0..A3, D0..D3 at 0..72, then eight i32 M0..M3, K, batch, x_f32, d_bf16_mask at 72..104). It is NOT a production image: the production launcher Gpu::launch_gemm_bf16_mfma_rows16 builds one params array and one KernargBlob and launches the HIP entries by name, and that single launch site is what the gate checks against the HIP declaration; nothing embeds the twin (kernels.rs must not name it), so it is not in pm_images. The gate only proves that the twin's embedded HSA metadata (read with the architecture-independent envelope reader) and the portable hipcc anchor declare the identical ABI as that HIP source, argument by argument, so a launch checked against the HIP declaration is also valid for the twin.

kernels/gemm_bf16_mfma_wide_gfx942_pm_gf.reason: Exact owner-pinned P1b wide device-ELF twin, not embedded by this artifact-only unit. All three HIP declarations, anchor metadata and PM metadata retain the same 104-byte kernarg layout: nine pointers at 0..72 and eight i32 values at 72..104. The live owner launcher commit must stack with this twin and pass the complete launcher ABI gate before landing; no unlaunched exemption is granted.

kernels/gemm_fp8b128_moe_grouped_bf16mfm.reason: Committed gfx942 PeaceMaker twin of the three production HIP entries of the FP8 block-128 grouped MoE BF16-MFMA GEMM: same symbol names and the same kernarg ABI as the hipcc anchor (grouped and _xbf16: 64 bytes = W ptr 0, expert_stride u64 8, tile_desc ptr 16, sorted_rows ptr 24, X ptr 32, Y ptr 40, then i32 R, K, x_row_div, n_exp at 48..64; tile_desc_pad16: 20 bytes = two pointers at 0 and 8, one i32 at 16). It is NOT a production image: nothing embeds the twin (kernels.rs must not name it), so it is not in pm_images. The gate only proves that the twin's embedded HSA metadata and the portable hipcc anchor declare the identical ABI as the HIP declarations; byte-exact behavior is proven by the hardware anchor-vs-twin oracle in crates/rdna-compute/examples/test_fp8_moe_gfx942.rs.

kernels/qwen4_g942_glue_elem_pm_gfx942.h.reason: gfx942 C elementwise-fold Route-A qualification twin: byte-identical full device ELF, exact HIP/HSA ABI and hash-bound hardware receipt. Land together with the owner kernel and checked live launcher; no production image or dispatch changes in this commit.

kernels/qwen4_g942_glue_moe_pm_gfx942.hx.reason: gfx942 C MoE glue Route-A qualification twin: byte-identical full device ELF and exact HIP/HSA ABI. Land with its owner kernel and checked live launcher; no production dispatch or obligation-class change.

kernels/qwen4_gdn_lanes_step_f32_gfx942_.reason: gfx942 GDN lanes Route-A qualification twin: byte-identical full device ELF and exact HIP/HSA ABI. Land with its owner kernel and checked live launcher; no production dispatch or obligation-class change.

crates/hipfire-runtime/examples/moe_nan_.reason: launch_raw launches a hip_bridge::Function handle with the raw kernarg bytes it is handed. It is exempt ONLY because every function that creates an OLD handle (load_old_image, K1Path::OldImage) and every direct caller, in both provenance scopes (the f1 scope here and the rc4b scope below), is pinned by token fingerprint, and each loads a separately loaded historical module (old_dir/old_ref), never the current embedded image. The gate proves that source origin, not the bytes of the external artifact. The NEW launchers (K1Path::Raw and K1Path::Dev in k1_run, which launch by symbol through Gpu::launch_kernel_blob / the production mq_i4_moe_gemv_slab launcher) are not exempt and remain checked launch sites.

scopes.reason: e8p_containment loads historical OLD images through cx.load_old_image from mandatory old_dir: rc4b on gfx1201/gfx1100, plus the pre-rc5 gfx1151 baseline 11411610be74647b1855e6e37fddcd1178ca7881. Re-audited upstream e95865cf1fd864f453956d0bddb2426e98bf33fc adds only the gfx1151 historical K2 basename in k2_old_stem and two diagnostic strings in run; Main authorized exactly those two fingerprint updates, with no handle or ABI change. The handles go to k1_run as K1Path::OldImage, which builds the pre-guard 88-byte k1_blob(.., None) and calls launch_raw (k1_phase, k1_chain); k2_gemm launches the OLD K2 handle through launch_raw with a 60-byte NT1 blob (five pointers and five i32). run, run_body, phase, k2_old_stem, k2_run, k2_pipeline, k2_phase and k2_chain remain the pinned selectors and drivers. NEW paths remain independently checked. The report records only an image digest, with no expected-hash check, so this gate proves the separately loaded old_dir source origin and pinned call chain, not historical artifact authenticity.
